newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB says to cut July debenture coupon to 2.55 pct.
newsitem.headline: NCB says to cut July debenture coupon to 2.55 pct.

text.p: Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) said on Wednesday it would cut the coupon rate for its five-year debentures to be issued this month to 2.55 percent from 2.75 percent in June.
NCB also said it would cut its long-term prime lending rate by the same 0.2 percentage point margin to 2.7 percent for July, effective from Thursday.
The prime rate, which is applied to loans of one year and longer to Japanese long-term credit banks' most creditworthy clients, is reviewed every month, reflecting market trends.
Bank debentures, which are issued monthly, are the long-term credit banks' major fund-raising tool.
The bank set the new coupon rate in light of current interest rate conditions and the bank's asset/liability management, an NCB spokesman said.
Traders said long-term credit banks usually refer to market yields of the last issued debentures to set the coupon rate of their new debentures.

But NCB's 2.75 percent June five-year debentures have not been traded in the secondary market since they were issued last month. That was mainly due to a cut in the volumes of the bank's recent issues, they said.

On Tuesday, the Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd, the largest of Japan's three long-term credit banks, said it would cut the coupon rate of its July five-year bank debentures to 1.8 percent from two percent, and its July long-term prime rate to 2.7 percent from 2.9 percent.
